relationships.subject: DkTx
relationships.evidence_quote: The DkTx toxin, derived from the venom of the Malaysian earthtiger tarantula, binds to the extracellular pore domain of TRPV1, locking the receptor open and causing pain

relationships.subject: RhTx
relationships.evidence_quote: Specifically, RhTx binds to the outer pore region of TRPV1 as a selective TRPV1 activator and does not affect other TRPV channels (TRPV2–4)

relationships.subject: APHC1-3
relationships.evidence_quote: APHCs enhance the TRPV1 response at low concentrations of capsaicin but block the response at high concentrations

relationships.subject: TRPV1 antagonists
relationships.evidence_quote: The knock out of TRPV1 in mice or TRPV1 antagonists induces prolonged hyperthermia, an undesired side effect, upon exposure to warm ambient temperature

relationships.subject: bradykinin
relationships.evidence_quote: Endogenous agonists include bioactive lipids, inflammatory soups (bradykinin and histamine)

key_findings: Venom peptides (DkTx, RhTx, BmP01, APHCs) bind the TRPV1 outer pore region to activate or inhibit the channel
Differences in outer pore movement could be exploited to design modality-specific TRPV1 inhibitors without hyperthermia
